name: Two distinct signature labels on both Signature-Input and Signature — verifier processes sig1 and does not reject the dictionaries
spec_reference: #adcp-rfc-9421-profile (One signature per request); #verifier-checklist-requests step 1 (duplicate-key rejection applies to repeated labels, not to distinct ones)
$comment: False-positive guard for negative/029 and 021: Signature-Input and Signature each carry two DISTINCT labels (sig1, sig2), which is legal. sig1 is a real Ed25519 signature over expected_signature_base; sig2 has a different covered-components set, a different nonce, and a well-formed 64-byte value that does not verify. Verifiers MUST process exactly one label (conventionally sig1) and ignore the rest; attempting sig2 and rejecting is non-conformant. Differs from 004-multiple-signature-labels only in sig2's signature bytes: 004 uses a run of 'A' (decodes to a 66-byte zero value, not a 64-byte signature), so a verifier that shape-validates every Signature member could pass 004 by luck; here the extra member is a correctly sized 64-byte signature. Signature generated with the test-ed25519-2026 private key from expected_signature_base.
